title: From brief to folio
lede: Each entry is one event. A short note and a long note use the same frame, and the frame is what the paginator is asked to keep together.

events.title: The brief is a list, not a layout
body: The job names a trim, a language, and the kinds of page required. It does not yet decide which sentence falls on a left-hand page.

events.title: The grid is written down
body: Margins, type size, and the gap between columns are recorded as tokens.
Nothing in the manuscript stores a millimetre value of its own. When the reference file is measured, the tokens move and these sentences stay.

events.title: The manuscript arrives in parts
body: Chapters come in as MDX. The chronology and the infographic come in as JSON. The order of the sheets is the manifest, not the alphabetical order of the files.

events.title: A figure is an object with a caption
body: The diagram is a file under assets. The caption is content. The component refuses a figure that has a source and no words describing it.

events.title: The first proof is allowed to be long
body: This event is deliberately longer than its neighbors. It has two paragraphs, and the second one keeps going so the sequence contains uneven measure: a single sentence in one entry, a short stack of lines in another, and this fuller note that would orphan its heading if the layout treated every paragraph as loose text in one column.

The event is one list item. The style asks the paginator not to split it. If a future event grows past the height of the text block, that request can no longer be honored, and the event has to be edited or the rule revisited. The limitation sits with the system rather than behind a sample that only uses even, tiny notes.

events.title: A margin is not a second story
body: Notes stay in the flow or in a designed region. This specimen does not yet run a side note into the margin.

events.title: Two files leave the same source
body: One PDF is for reading. One is a print layout with bleed and crop marks. Neither file is a silent conversion to a print standard. The chronology ends where a handoff to a printer would begin, and that handoff is still a decision, not a command in this repository.
